shaka-gruendet-zulu-reich#text: Shaka, a son of the Zulu chief Senzangakhona, first served in the army of the Mthethwa ruler Dingiswayo and, with his support, took over the leadership of the then small Zulu in 1816. He organized the warriors into age-based regiments that lived in their own barracks and relied on disciplined close combat with a short stabbing spear and a large shield. Within a few years he subjugated or drove out numerous neighbors and created a centrally governed kingdom in present-day KwaZulu-Natal. His rule was marked by great harshness; in 1828 he was murdered by his half-brothers. The image of Shaka was later heavily embellished both by European authors and in Zulu nationalism.
mfecane-im-suedlichen-afrika#summary: Wars and migrations transform the political map of southern Africa and lead to the founding of new states.
mfecane-im-suedlichen-afrika#text: In the early 19th century, wars over land, cattle and trade routes in southeastern Africa set off a chain of flights and conquests. Groups such as the Ndebele under Mzilikazi, the Gaza under Soshangane or the Ngoni under Zwangendaba moved far to the north, some as far as Lake Malawi and Lake Tanganyika. At the same time Moshoeshoe gathered refugees on the mountain plateau of Thaba Bosiu and founded the kingdom of the Basotho, from which Lesotho emerged. Many people lost their lives or their homes. The causes are still debated today: besides the rise of the Zulu, historians also point to droughts, population pressure and the slave and ivory trade.
radama-vertrag-mit-grossbritannien#title: Radama I of Madagascar allies with Britain
radama-vertrag-mit-grossbritannien#summa: The Merina king concludes a treaty with Britain, renounces the export of slaves and opens his kingdom to schools and missions.
radama-vertrag-mit-grossbritannien#text: The Merina kingdom in the highlands of Madagascar had been united around Antananarivo under King Andrianampoinimerina. His son Radama I concluded a treaty with the British governor of Mauritius in 1817: he banned the export of slaves and in return received weapons, instructors and recognition as king of Madagascar. With this support he subjugated large parts of the island. From 1820 missionaries of the London Missionary Society founded schools and wrote Malagasy in the Latin alphabet for the first time. After Radama's death in 1828 his widow Ranavalona I turned against European influence.
san-martin-ueberquert-die-anden#summary: José de San Martín leads the Army of the Andes across the high mountains and defeats the Spaniards at Chacabuco.
san-martin-ueberquert-die-anden#text: San Martín planned to attack Spanish power in Peru not across the highlands but via Chile and the sea. In January 1817 his army of about 5,000 men crossed the Andes over several passes, a march over passes partly higher than 3,000 metres. On 12 February it defeated the royalists at Chacabuco, and Bernardo O'Higgins took over the government of Chile. After the victory at Maipú in 1818 Chile was secure. From there San Martín sailed to Peru in 1820 and proclaimed its independence in Lima in 1821.
bolivar-unabhaengigkeit-suedamerikas#tit: Bolívar and the independence of South America
bolivar-unabhaengigkeit-suedamerikas#sum: Simón Bolívar defeats the Spanish at Boyacá and founds the republic of Gran Colombia.
bolivar-unabhaengigkeit-suedamerikas#tex: From 1810 the Spanish colonies of America fought for their independence, encouraged by the example of the United States and by the weakness of Spain under Napoleonic occupation. In 1819 Bolívar crossed the Andes with his army and defeated the Spanish at Boyacá, whereupon Gran Colombia arose out of the present-day states of Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama. In the south José de San Martín liberated Argentina and Chile; in 1824, with the battle of Ayacucho, the last Spanish stronghold in Peru fell.
griechischer-unabhaengigkeitskrieg#summa: A Greek uprising leads, with the help of Britain, France and Russia, to the first independent state on Ottoman soil in Europe.
griechischer-unabhaengigkeitskrieg#text: In March 1821 Greeks rose against Ottoman rule in the Peloponnese and the Danubian principalities. Both sides waged the war with massacres, for example at Tripolitsa in 1821 and on Chios in 1822. European philhellenes such as Lord Byron supported the insurgents. From 1825 Egyptian troops under Ibrahim Pasha threatened to crush the uprising, but in 1827 British, French and Russian ships destroyed the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at Navarino. In the London Protocol of 1830 Greece was recognized as an independent state.
mexikanische-unabhaengigkeit#summary: Eleven years after the call to arms by the priest Hidalgo, New Spain separates from Spain and becomes independent as Mexico.
mexikanische-unabhaengigkeit#text: On 16 September 1810 the parish priest Miguel Hidalgo called on the population in the village of Dolores to rise against Spanish colonial rule; tens of thousands of indigenous people and mestizos followed him, but they were defeated in 1811, and Hidalgo was executed. His successor José María Morelos carried on the struggle, called a congress, and in 1815 likewise died before a firing squad. When a liberal revolution broke out in Spain in 1820, the royal officer Agustín de Iturbide changed sides and agreed with the rebel leader Vicente Guerrero on the Plan of Iguala, which promised independence, Catholicism, and equality for all inhabitants. On 27 September 1821 the army entered Mexico City; Iturbide had himself crowned emperor but was overthrown in 1823, and in 1824 Mexico gave itself a republican constitution. 16 September is still the national holiday today.
unabhaengigkeit-brasiliens#summary: Crown Prince Pedro declares Brazil independent of Portugal and becomes the country's first emperor.
unabhaengigkeit-brasiliens#text: After King John VI returned to Lisbon, the Portuguese Cortes wanted to make Brazil a dependent colony again. His son Pedro, who had stayed behind as regent, resisted and on 7 September 1822 proclaimed independence on the banks of the Ipiranga near São Paulo. In December he was crowned emperor as Pedro I. Unlike Spanish America, Brazil did not break up into several states but remained united as a monarchy. Slavery and the power of the great landowners, however, remained untouched.
eisenbahn-stockton-darlington#summary: The first public railway with a steam locomotive runs in northern England.
eisenbahn-stockton-darlington#text: On 27 September 1825 the locomotive Locomotion No. 1, built by George Stephenson, pulled a train carrying coal and passengers over the roughly 40 kilometers between Stockton and Darlington. The line was the first public railway to use steam locomotives permanently. Within a few decades a network of rails covered Europe and North America and made the transport of goods and people faster and cheaper than ever before.
aufloesung-der-janitscharen#summary: Sultan Mahmud II has the rebellious Janissary corps shot down and dissolved, clearing the way for a modern army.
aufloesung-der-janitscharen#text: In the spring of 1826 Mahmud II announced a new corps drilled on European lines. When the Janissaries revolted against it in Istanbul on 15 June 1826, the sultan had their barracks shelled with artillery; thousands were killed. On 17 June the centuries-old corps was dissolved and the Bektashi order associated with it was banned. The government called the event "the Auspicious Incident". A new army took the place of the Janissaries and became the core of later reforms.
julirevolution-1830#summary: In three days of fighting at the barricades, Paris overthrows the Bourbon king Charles X; Louis-Philippe becomes the Citizen King, and the revolution has effects in Belgium, Poland, and Germany.
julirevolution-1830#text: King Charles X tried to extend the power of the crown against parliament and on 25 July 1830 issued ordinances that abolished freedom of the press, restricted the franchise, and dissolved the chamber that had just been elected. Journalists, students, craftsmen, and workers thereupon put up barricades, and in the three glorious days from 27 to 29 July they captured the city hall and the Louvre; around 800 insurgents died. Charles X fled to England, and the liberal citizenry, with Lafayette's support, installed the Duke of Orléans as Louis-Philippe I, King of the French, who adopted the tricolor and swore an oath to the constitution. The revolution set off the revolt of Belgium against the Netherlands, the Polish November Uprising against Russia, and unrest in several German states; Delacroix's painting Liberty Leading the People became its emblem.
hambacher-fest#summary: Around 30,000 people gather at Hambach Castle to demand freedom, German unity, and understanding among nations; it is the largest political rally of the Vormärz.
hambacher-fest#text: After the July Revolution, resentment over censorship, taxes, and arbitrary policing had also built up in the Bavarian Palatinate; the Carlsbad Decrees of 1819 had placed the press and the universities throughout Germany under supervision. The journalists Philipp Jakob Siebenpfeiffer and Johann Georg August Wirth issued an invitation to a popular festival, and from 27 to 30 May 1832 craftsmen, peasants, students, and townspeople, among them many women as well as Polish and French guests, marched under black-red-gold flags to Hambach Castle near Neustadt an der Weinstraße. The speakers demanded freedom of the press, a constitution, national unity, and a Europe of free peoples; an uprising, however, was not resolved upon. The German Confederation responded with a ban on political associations and assemblies and had the organizers put on trial. The festival is regarded as the cradle of German democracy, and black-red-gold became the national colors in 1848 and 1919.
abschaffung-sklaverei-britisches-empire#: The abolition of slavery in the British Empire
The British parliament resolves to free around 800,000 enslaved people in the colonies.

After Great Britain had already banned the slave trade in 1807, abolitionists such as William Wilberforce, mass petitions, and slave revolts in the Caribbean brought about the abolition of slavery itself. The Slavery Abolition Act of 1833 came into force on 1 August 1834; the slaveholders received 20 million pounds in compensation, while those set free had at first to go on working for years as so-called apprentices. France followed in 1848, the United States in 1865, Brazil only in 1888. From then on the British fleet hunted slave ships in the Atlantic, which at the same time served as a justification for the extension of British power in Africa.
tanzimat-edikt-von-guelhane#title: Edict of Gülhane and the beginning of the Tanzimat
tanzimat-edikt-von-guelhane#summary: A solemn edict promises all subjects security of life, honour and property as well as equality before the law, regardless of their religion.
tanzimat-edikt-von-guelhane#text: On 3 November 1839, a few months after the death of Mahmud II, Foreign Minister Mustafa Reşid Pasha read out an edict of the young sultan Abdülmecid I in the Gülhane park below the Topkapı Palace. It promised protection of life, honour and property, a regular tax system, orderly conscription and equal rights for Muslims and non-Muslims. This began the Tanzimat, the "reorderings", with new law codes, ministries and state schools. The Reform Edict of 1856 confirmed the equality. The reforms strengthened the central state but also met with resistance.
erster-opiumkrieg#summary: Great Britain forces China open to trade with gunboats.
erster-opiumkrieg#text: British merchants sold large quantities of opium from India to China and thereby balanced their trade. When the Chinese government stopped the smuggling in 1839 and had opium destroyed, Great Britain sent a fleet. In the Treaty of Nanking of 1842, China had to cede Hong Kong, open five ports, and pay heavy indemnities. The war began what is known as China's century of humiliation.
sansibar-wird-sultanssitz#title: Zanzibar becomes the seat of the Sultan of Oman
sansibar-wird-sultanssitz#summary: Sultan Said moves his residence from Muscat to Zanzibar, which becomes the center of East African trade.
sansibar-wird-sultanssitz#text: Since the late 17th century the Omani sultans had driven the Portuguese from the Swahili coast. Around 1840 Sultan Said bin Sultan made the island of Zanzibar his main seat and promoted the cultivation of cloves there on plantations worked by enslaved people. Caravans of Swahili-speaking and Arab traders pushed as far as the Great Lakes and into the Congo and brought ivory and captives to the coast. Zanzibar thus became the largest slave market in East Africa. Only in 1873 was Sultan Barghash forced by British pressure to close the slave market.
weberaufstand-schlesien#summary: Impoverished handloom weavers rise against the manufacturers and are put down by the Prussian military.
weberaufstand-schlesien#text: The cotton weavers in the Owl Mountains of Silesia could no longer keep up with English machine-made cloth and received ever lower wages from the merchant clothiers. On 4 June 1844 hundreds of weavers in Peterswaldau and Langenbielau marched to the houses of the manufacturers and destroyed machines and account books. Prussian soldiers fired into the crowd, eleven people died, and the leaders were sentenced to the penitentiary. The uprising made the social question a subject of debate throughout Germany; Heinrich Heine wrote the poem The Silesian Weavers, and Gerhart Hauptmann the drama The Weavers in 1892.
irische-hungersnot#summary: Potato blight destroys the harvests; around a million Irish starve to death, and further millions emigrate.
irische-hungersnot#text: The poor rural population of Ireland lived almost entirely on potatoes. When from 1845 onward a fungus destroyed the harvests for several years in succession, hundreds of thousands starved or died of typhus and cholera, while grain and cattle continued to be exported to England. The British government trusted in the free market and helped too late and too little. The population of Ireland fell from around 8.5 million to 6.5 million in the year 1851; millions of Irish emigrated to North America, and the memory of the famine fueled Irish nationalism.
mexikanisch-amerikanischer-krieg#summary: After the annexation of Texas by the United States, Mexico loses large parts of its territory in a war with its northern neighbour.
mexikanisch-amerikanischer-krieg#text: Texas had broken away from Mexico in 1836 and was admitted to the United States in 1845; a dispute over the border led to war in 1846. US troops occupied California and New Mexico, landed at Veracruz and captured Mexico City in September 1847. In the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo of 1848 Mexico ceded the territories of today's states of California, Nevada, Utah and parts of further states in return for a payment of 15 million dollars. For Mexico the defeat was a national trauma. The young cadets who fell defending Chapultepec are still honoured today as the Boy Heroes.
kastenkrieg-in-yucatan#summary: Maya on the Yucatán peninsula rise up against land seizures and exploitation and hold a territory of their own for decades.
kastenkrieg-in-yucatan#text: The expansion of sugar and cattle farming had taken land from the Maya villages in eastern Yucatán, and heavy dues drove many peasants into debt. In the summer of 1847 an uprising began that pushed the white and mestizo inhabitants back to the edge of the capital Mérida. After counter-attacks the rebels withdrew into the forests of the east and founded an independent territory around Chan Santa Cruz. Only in 1901 did the Mexican army occupy the town. The war cost tens of thousands of people their lives.
kommunistisches-manifest#summary: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish the programmatic text of the communist movement.
kommunistisches-manifest#text: In February 1848, shortly before the outbreak of the European revolutions, the Manifesto of the Communist Party appeared in London. In it Marx and Engels described history as a succession of class struggles and predicted that the proletariat would overthrow the bourgeoisie. The text ends with the call, workers of all countries, unite. It became one of the most influential political texts in history.
maerzrevolution-1848#title: The March Revolution of 1848 and the Frankfurt National Assembly
maerzrevolution-1848#summary: A wave of revolution sweeps across Europe; the first all-German parliament assembles in the Paulskirche in Frankfurt.
maerzrevolution-1848#text: After the February Revolution in Paris, people in Vienna, Berlin, and many German states demanded freedom of the press, constitutions, and national unity in March 1848; Metternich fled, and in Berlin hundreds of citizens died in fighting at the barricades. The National Assembly elected to the Paulskirche adopted basic rights and a constitution for a German empire. When the Prussian king Frederick William IV refused the imperial crown in 1849, the revolution failed, and the princes restored the old order.
krimkrieg#summary: Britain and France fight alongside the Ottoman Empire against Russia to prevent its advance towards the Straits.
krimkrieg#text: A dispute over the holy places in Jerusalem and Russia's claim to protect the Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire led to war in 1853. After the Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman fleet at Sinope in November 1853, Britain and France entered the war in 1854. The fighting concentrated on the siege of Sevastopol in the Crimea, where epidemics killed more soldiers than weapons; in the military hospital at Üsküdar, Florence Nightingale set new standards in nursing. In the Peace of Paris in 1856 the Black Sea was neutralized and the Ottoman Empire was admitted to the Concert of Europe. To finance the war it took out its first foreign loans.
tewodros-ii-einigt-aethiopien#summary: The coronation of Tewodros II ends the Era of the Princes, during which Ethiopia had broken up into rival regional lordships.
tewodros-ii-einigt-aethiopien#text: Since the late 18th century powerful regional lords had ruled in Ethiopia, while the emperors were mere figureheads. Kassa Hailu, a warlord from the west of the country, defeated his rivals and had himself crowned emperor as Tewodros II in 1855. He wanted to centralize the empire, build a standing army and modernize with European technology, but met with resistance from the nobility and the church. When he held British envoys captive, Britain sent an army that stormed his fortress of Magdala in 1868. Tewodros took his own life and is today regarded as a pioneer of modern Ethiopia.
reformgesetze-und-verfassung-1857#title: Juárez, the Reform Laws and the Constitution of 1857
reformgesetze-und-verfassung-1857#summar: Mexican Liberals curb the power of the Church and the army; the dispute over this leads to the Reform War.
reformgesetze-und-verfassung-1857#text: After the fall of General Santa Anna in 1855, Liberal politicians abolished the special courts of the clergy and the military and forced the Church and communities to sell their landed property. The Constitution of 1857 guaranteed basic rights such as freedom of the press and of teaching. Conservatives and large parts of the Church rejected it, and a three-year civil war followed, the Reform War. Benito Juárez led the Liberal side as president, decreed the separation of church and state and entered Mexico City victorious at the beginning of 1861. The sale of communal land, however, disadvantaged many Indigenous villages.
sepoy-aufstand-indien#summary: Indian soldiers mutiny against the British East India Company; afterward the Crown takes over the rule of India.
sepoy-aufstand-indien#text: The trigger in May 1857 was the rumor that the cartridges of new rifles were greased with beef and pork fat, which offended Hindus and Muslims alike among the native soldiers, the sepoys. The mutiny at Meerut grew into an uprising across northern India; the rebels took Delhi and proclaimed the old Mughal emperor as their ruler. British troops put down the revolt by 1858 with extreme severity. The East India Company was dissolved, India was placed directly under the British Crown, and in 1876 Queen Victoria assumed the title Empress of India.
darwin-entstehung-der-arten#title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
darwin-entstehung-der-arten#summary: Charles Darwin explains the diversity of life through evolution and natural selection.
darwin-entstehung-der-arten#text: On 24 November 1859 Darwin's book On the Origin of Species appeared in London, and its first edition sold out the same day. Drawing on observations from his voyage around the world on the Beagle and on decades of research, Darwin showed that species are not unchangeable but develop from common ancestors through natural selection. The theory contradicted the literal reading of the biblical account of creation and set off fierce debates. It became the foundation of modern biology, but it was also misused to justify racism and imperialism through what is known as Social Darwinism.
amerikanischer-buergerkrieg#summary: The Northern and Southern states of the USA fight over the unity of the Union and the abolition of slavery.
amerikanischer-buergerkrieg#text: After the election of Abraham Lincoln, eleven Southern states left the Union because they saw slavery under threat. The war claimed more than 600,000 lives and was the first in which the railroad, the telegraph and industrial weapons production played a decisive role. Slavery was abolished by the Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 and the Thirteenth Amendment of 1865; the surrender of the Southern states preserved the unity of the United States.
franzoesische-intervention-in-mexiko#sum: Napoleon III installs the Habsburg Maximilian as emperor in Mexico; after the French withdraw he is executed.
franzoesische-intervention-in-mexiko#tex: When Mexico suspended its debt payments in 1861, European troops landed; France used the situation to set up an empire dependent on Paris. On 5 May 1862 the Mexican army at first defeated the French at Puebla, but in 1863 Mexico City fell. In 1864 Archduke Maximilian of Austria accepted the imperial crown. Juárez continued the republican government in the north, and after the end of the American Civil War Napoleon III withdrew his troops. In 1867 Maximilian was captured at Querétaro and shot.
gruendung-rotes-kreuz#summary: An organization to care for wounded soldiers is created in Geneva on the initiative of Henry Dunant.
gruendung-rotes-kreuz#text: In 1859 Henry Dunant had witnessed the suffering of the wounded after the Battle of Solferino, and in his book A Memory of Solferino he called for voluntary relief societies and an international agreement to protect the wounded. In February 1863 he founded, together with four other citizens of Geneva, the committee from which the International Committee of the Red Cross emerged; in October the first international conference met. On 22 August 1864 twelve states signed the first Geneva Convention, which placed medical personnel, field hospitals and the wounded under the protection of the red cross on a white ground. This marked the beginning of modern international humanitarian law.
paraguay-krieg#summary: Paraguay fights the Triple Alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay and suffers devastating losses.
paraguay-krieg#text: In 1864 the Paraguayan president Francisco Solano López intervened in a conflict in Uruguay and found himself at war with Brazil and Argentina, which allied with Uruguay in 1865. It became the bloodiest war in the history of South America. Battles, hunger and epidemics killed a large share of Paraguay's population, above all of its men; estimates vary widely. The war ended in 1870 with the death of López. Paraguay lost territory to Brazil and Argentina and was weakened for decades.
zehnjaehriger-krieg-auf-kuba#title: The Ten Years' War in Cuba
zehnjaehriger-krieg-auf-kuba#summary: Cuban planters and freed people rise against Spanish rule; the first war of independence ends without victory.
zehnjaehriger-krieg-auf-kuba#text: On 10 October 1868 the landowner Carlos Manuel de Céspedes freed his slaves at his sugar mill La Demajagua and called for a fight for independence. Whites, free Black people and formerly enslaved people fought together, above all in the east of the island; Antonio Maceo rose to become one of the best-known commanders. Spain deployed large armies, and the rebels were divided among themselves. In 1878 the Pact of Zanjón ended the war without bringing independence or the complete abolition of slavery. Slavery in Cuba ended only in 1886.
meiji-restauration#summary: Japan ends the rule of the shoguns and modernizes along Western lines.
meiji-restauration#text: After American warships had forced Japan to open up in 1853, reform-minded samurai overthrew the shogunate in 1868 and placed the young Emperor Meiji at the head of the state. The new government abolished the system of social estates, introduced compulsory schooling and military service, and had railways, factories and a modern fleet built. Within a single generation Japan became the first industrial power in Asia and in 1905 even defeated Russia.
eroeffnung-suezkanal#summary: The canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea shortens the sea route to Asia by thousands of kilometers.
eroeffnung-suezkanal#text: Under the direction of the Frenchman Ferdinand de Lesseps, tens of thousands of Egyptian laborers dug a canal 160 kilometers long through the Isthmus of Suez over ten years. Ships sailing from Europe to India no longer had to travel around Africa. In 1875 Britain bought the Egyptian shares in the canal and occupied the country in 1882 in order to secure the lifeline of its colonial empire.
gruendung-deutsches-kaiserreich#summary: After the victory over France, William I is proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles.
gruendung-deutsches-kaiserreich#text: In three wars against Denmark, Austria and France, Otto von Bismarck had united the German states under Prussian leadership. On 18 January 1871 the Prussian king William I was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. The new empire was a constitutional monarchy with universal male suffrage for the Reichstag, but with a strong position for the emperor and the chancellor. It quickly became the leading industrial power on the continent.
osmanischer-staatsbankrott#title: State bankruptcy and the debt administration
osmanischer-staatsbankrott#summary: Overindebted, the Ottoman Empire suspends its payments; European creditors take control of important state revenues.
osmanischer-staatsbankrott#text: Since the first loan of 1854 the government had taken out ever new credits in London and Paris, often on unfavourable terms, to pay for the army, reforms and the court. After bad harvests and an international financial crisis, it declared in October 1875 that it would pay only half of the interest. In 1881 Sultan Abdülhamid II established the Ottoman Public Debt Administration by the Decree of Muharrem, in which representatives of the creditors sat. It collected the revenues from salt, tobacco, silk, stamp duties and fishing. The empire thereby lost part of its financial independence.
osmanische-verfassung-1876#summary: Under Grand Vizier Midhat Pasha the Ottoman Empire receives a constitution and an elected parliament.
osmanische-verfassung-1876#text: Reform-minded officials and the group of the Young Ottomans called for a constitution in order to unite the empire and forestall European interference. Sultan Abdülhamid II proclaimed the constitution shaped by Midhat Pasha, the Kanun-ı Esasi, on 23 December 1876. In March 1877 the first parliament met, in which Muslims, Christians and Jews sat. But Midhat had already been banished in February, and in February 1878 the sultan prorogued parliament indefinitely, citing the war with Russia. The constitution formally remained valid and was put back into force in 1908.
russisch-osmanischer-krieg-und-berliner-: Russo-Ottoman War and the Congress of Berlin
After the defeat by Russia the great powers reorganize the Balkans at the Congress of Berlin; Serbia, Montenegro and Romania become independent.

After the bloody suppression of an uprising in Bulgaria in 1876, Russia declared war on the Ottomans in 1877 and, after a long siege of Plevna, advanced to the outskirts of Istanbul. The Treaty of San Stefano in March 1878 provided for a large Bulgaria, which Britain and Austria-Hungary rejected. At the Congress of Berlin, chaired by Bismarck, Serbia, Montenegro and Romania became independent and Bulgaria an autonomous principality. Austria-Hungary occupied Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Britain took over Cyprus. Hundreds of thousands of Muslims fled from the Balkans to Anatolia.
